data.title: French finance ministry expects 2026 deficit of 5.4%, with debt rising to nearly 120% of GDP
data.description:
France's debt is expected to reach 119.3% of output in 2026, with the year likely to end with a budget deficit of 5.4%, the finance ministry said on Saturday.

The finance ministry expects the debt-to-GDP ratio to reach 121.7% in 2027 and the deficit to narrow to 5.0%, it said in a declaration to the High Council of Public Finance, the body tasked with evaluating revenue and expenditure forecasts in the government's budget proposal.

In 2025, France's debt-to-GDP ratio was 115.7%.

data.title: Arthur Hayes Says Crypto Didn't Need 'Nonsense' CLARITY Act - Just A Rate Hike, Bitcoin Tops $81K
data.description:
Key points:
  • Arthur Hayes said on Friday that the Federal Reserve's rate hike, not crypto legislation, was what lifted Bitcoin this week.
  • Grayscale's head of research called the same hike a mid-cycle adjustment unlikely to move crypto markets.
  • Bitcoin traded above $81,000 on Saturday, days after the Senate blocked the CLARITY Act.

As Bitcoin (BTC) traded above $81,000 on Saturday, Flop Labs CEO Arthur Hayes dismissed the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act (CLARITY Act) as "nonsense" and said crypto needed the Federal Reserve's rate hike, not the bill.

"See, we didn't need some nonsense piece of crypto regulation, Clarity Act, just a rate hike that puts more dollars in the hands of rich people to consume more financial assets," Hayes wrote in a post on X on Friday.

Bitcoin’s price traded at about $81,322, edging up over 3%. The token slipped to the $ 75,000 range on Wednesday, after the bill stalled in the Senate the day before, and has steadily increased since then.

On Stocktwits, the retail sentiment around BTC remained in the ‘bearish’ zone, while chatter around it stayed at ‘normal’ levels over the past day.

The Rate Hike

The rate decision Hayes credited came a day after the Senate vote. The Federal Open Market Committee voted 12-0 on Wednesday to raise the target range for the federal funds rate by a quarter point to 3.75% to 4%. It was the central bank's first increase since July 2023.

"Inflation remains elevated," the committee said. It added that the move would support a timelier return to its 2% goal.

Higher rates tend to weigh on assets that pay no income, because investors can earn more by holding cash instead. Hayes argued the reverse, saying the hike channels more money to wealthy holders of financial assets.

Grayscale Sees Limited Impact

However, not everyone reached the same conclusion. Grayscale's head of research, Zach Pandl, wrote in a note published on Thursday that the hike was unlikely to drive major changes in crypto markets.

Pandl described the move as a mid-cycle adjustment rather than a cyclical policy shift. He pointed to March 1997, when the Federal Reserve delivered a similar one-off increase, and the Nasdaq (NDAQ) bull market continued. The one or two hikes expected in 2026 were unlikely to change capital allocation much, he said.

He did flag one direct effect, though. Stablecoin issuers such as Circle (CRCL) and Tether (USDT) earned higher revenues when cash rates rose, Pandl said. Higher rates on tokenized bonds and money market funds could also draw flows onchain.

Bill Failed Days Earlier

What made Hayes' framing sharp was what the industry lost that week. The Senate did not agree to a motion to invoke cloture on the CLARITY Act on Tuesday, by a vote of 49-50. The motion needed 60 votes. The defeat was treated across the sector as a setback, with Coinbase (COIN) CEO Brian Armstrong calling the outcome a disappointment and saying the industry could not wait on Congress any longer.

data.title: Porsche could face another 4,000 job cuts, Handelsblatt reports
data.description:
Volkswagen's sweeping turnaround plan foresees more than 4,000 further job cuts at Porsche , German business daily Handelsblatt reported on Saturday, following a profit warning linked to problems at the sports car subsidiary.

Files documenting a recent agreement by Volkswagen's supervisory board to usher in the German auto group's largest restructuring yet propose a reduction of "about 4,100 employees" at the brand, addressing an overhead shortfall of some €700 million ($803.8 million), according to Handelsblatt.

The newspaper said the cuts would be "in addition to existing agreements".

In July, Porsche management and labour representatives agreed to an additional 5,000 layoffs on top of 4,000 determined earlier, bringing the scope of currently agreed job cuts at the Stuttgart-based 911 maker to around one in five by 2035.

Volkswagen could not immediately be reached for comment. A Porsche spokesperson declined to comment on the reported plans of Volkswagen's supervisory board.

The parent company can only recommend, but not mandate, such measures at Porsche.

Volkswagen on Friday revised down its full-year margin target, now hoping for 1% at best rather than a previous range of 4.0-5.5%.

The revision was due in large part to a writedown at Porsche, where CEO Michael Leiters is under pressure to deliver a comeback strategy following a collapse in China sales and a costly reversal of the carmaker's EV strategy.

($1 = 0.8709 euros)

data.title: Stocks face a growing list of threats - so why are investors staying so calm?
data.description:
By Isabel Wang

Investors are well aware of the risks, but they have simply decided none are significant enough to force them out of the market

Stocks have every reason to sell off, but they refuse to budge

On the surface, this looks like the easiest quarter stocks have had in years.

The S&P 500 is up modestly in recent months and moving in a narrow lane, while the Cboe Volatility Index - known as Wall Street's "fear gauge" - is snoozing near its lowest level of the year. That's despite the Iran war pushing oil prices above $100 a barrel, a new Federal Reserve's interest-rate hike and artificial-intelligence executives publicly begging their own industry to slow down.

The stock market's reaction to all of it? A shrug.

All three major indexes on the U.S. stock market have been churning sideways in the third quarter of 2026 - with the S&P 500 SPX up 2% through Friday, the Dow Jones Industrial Average DJIA off 1.2% and the Nasdaq Composite COMP up 1.2% in the period, according to FactSet data. More notably, despite all the macroeconomic and geopolitical drama, the S&P 500 has not seen a 2% daily move in either direction since June 5.

Even the options market, which is inherently more aggressive and forward-looking than the equity market, isn't panicking either. The Cboe Volatility Index VIX closed Friday at 14.81, just above its 2026 closing low of 14.25, hit on Aug. 14. A VIX reading below 20 is seen as signaling a calm, stable stock market where investors expect low volatility over the next 30 days.

"The 'Spider-Man' market is again climbing 'a wall of worry,'" Steve Sosnick, chief strategist at Interactive Brokers, told MarketWatch on Friday. "Investors are not ready to give up on stocks. They are willing to take some trading profits occasionally when markets rally, but they're not really willing to part with their favorite shares even though they are seeing some erosion."

The erosion isn't visible from the surface, but the broader market is facing a growing list of risks.

First, the Federal Reserve has just begun a new monetary-tightening cycle, delivering its first rate hike in more than three years earlier this week. Oil prices (CL00) (CL.1) (BRN00) above $100 a barrel, driven by the Iran war, also remain front and center, pushing gasoline prices across the country above an average of $4.47 a gallon and squeezing consumer budgets. Meanwhile, recent calls from industry leaders to slow the development of advanced AI have triggered a temporary plunge in global chip stocks DRAM.

Looming in the background are rising long-term Treasury yields, with the benchmark 10-year rate BX:TMUBMUSD10Y having climbed above what many view as the critical 5% level. Higher yields make borrowing more expensive for consumers and businesses, putting pressure on stock valuations and increasing the cost of government debt.

To be sure, any one of these headlines could, on its own, be enough to move the stock market significantly. Instead, stocks have spent the past three months locked in a relatively narrow trading range. Market analysts say investors are well aware of the risks in front of them; they have simply decided, at least for now, that none are significant enough to force them out of the market.

"The market is now saying, 'I don't know,'" said Mike Treacy, head of risk at Apex Fintech Solutions. "On one hand, you have a very healthy growing economy. On the other hand, that economy is being financed by the AI build-out, and then interest rates are going higher, so it causes you to pause to the upside."

Mark Hackett, chief market strategist at Nationwide's Investment Management Group, said neither bulls nor bears have been able to "gain a clear advantage" since May, with inflation and rate uncertainty balanced against continued strong earnings growth.

"The Fed's first rate hike in three years confirmed that inflation, not growth, is again the central policy risk, and the lack of equity-market reaction suggests investors agree with that path and it was well communicated," Hackett said in emailed commentary.

Robust corporate earnings so far this year have indeed provided the fundamental support for major indexes to trade in record territory. This profit engine has helped absorb significant macro headwinds and keep equity valuations anchored.

"Investors have decided that earnings are what matter, and earnings do matter," said Sosnick at Interactive Brokers. "That's why the upside in stocks eventually hinges upon stocks' ability to deliver on increasingly rosy earnings expectations - not just for the next quarter or two, but for the quarters to come."

But some are still hedging their bets rather than rushing for the exits. Apex's Treacy pointed to a significant decrease in speculative trading in September, with the notional trading volume in U.S.-listed leveraged ETFs projected to reach just $24 billion this month, down from nearly $52 billion in June, according to data compiled by Apex.

"The tape has changed in that there is less speculation than there was in the first half of the year - and that puts us in 'Nowheresville,' where you have a healthy economy [and] a healthy job market, but also interest rates at extreme levels and oil at elevated levels," Treacy told MarketWatch in a phone interview on Friday.

U.S. stocks closed Friday mostly lower for the week. The Dow was off 1.7% on the week, while the S&P 500 fell 0.1% and the Nasdaq gained 0.7%, according to FactSet.

-Isabel Wang

data.title: IMF tells EU ministers AI could boost growth but increase economic strains
data.description:
Key points:
  • IMF paper says AI could raise European productivity around 1% over five years
  • Around 60% of workers in advanced European economies hold jobs highly exposed to AI
  • Europe's data centres consume roughly 3% of continent's electricity, IMF paper says

By Jan Strupczewski

Artificial intelligence could lift European productivity by about 1% over five years, but risks widening inequality, straining power networks and increasing dependence on foreign technology unless governments deepen economic integration, an International Monetary Fund paper said.

The background note, prepared for an informal meeting of European Union finance ministers in Dublin on September 18-19, said the benefits and costs of AI were likely to be distributed unevenly across countries, regions and workers.

It said completing the EU single market would help spread AI adoption and its gains more evenly across the 27-nation bloc.

The paper echoes concerns raised by former European Central Bank President Mario Draghi and the European Commission that Europe's fragmented capital, labour and energy markets are holding back investment and innovation.

The IMF estimated that around 60% of workers in advanced European economies are employed in occupations highly exposed to AI. While some could become more productive through AI tools, others faced displacement as routine tasks become automated, it said, particularly in jobs where AI is more likely to replace labour than complement it.

The paper said Europe's data centres already consume roughly 3% of the continent's electricity and that demand would rise sharply as AI use expands. Major technology hubs such as Frankfurt, London, Amsterdam, Paris and Dublin are among the areas most exposed, with data-centre clusters already putting pressure on local power networks.

To address that, the EU should invest in cross-border grid infrastructure and deepen integration o.f the European energy market, the IMF said.

The paper also warned that Europe risks developing another strategic dependency because the US and China dominate the development of AI models. It said Europe would need significant investment in its own AI industry to avoid becoming reliant on foreign technology.

AI's gains are also likely to be unevenly distributed across and within the EU, the paper said. More advanced economies are expected to benefit disproportionately because they are better prepared for and more exposed to the technology.

data.title: Canada optimistic about concluding trade talks with India by year-end, minister says
data.description:
By Ira Dugal

Canada is optimistic about concluding negotiations on a comprehensive economic partnership agreement (CEPA) with India by year-end, the country's minister for international trade said on Saturday.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney had previously said during a trip to New Delhi in March that the two countries would aim to agree a free trade pact by the end of the year.

"I'm feeling very, very optimistic and energetic that we can get it done in the coming months," Canadian Trade Minister Maninder Sidhu told Reuters in an interview during a visit to India's financial capital Mumbai.

Indian trade negotiators are expected to be in Canada next month and leaders from the two countries are likely to meet on the sidelines of the G-20 gathering in December, Sidhu said.

One main area of discussion is the energy sector. A Shell-led LNG ‌export facility launched in Canada last year and the country has five more projects in various phases of development.

"We're having conversations with Indian firms on how they can access those projects, but also how they can invest and secure supply in those projects," Sidhu said, declining to share further details.

Beyond liquefied natural gas, both countries are looking to expand cooperation in nuclear energy, where India is looking to significantly boost capacity.

"Canada has a long history in the nuclear industry, and I do see a lot of benefit for Canadian companies and industries to help build up a supply chain here in India," Sidhu said.

Sidhu said, without giving any further details, that a number of large Indian business houses from Reliance Industries to Mahindra and Mahindra and the JSW Group are exploring investments in critical mineral projects in Canada as a way to secure supply chains.

Companies are looking at ways to make co-investments as supply chains are getting weaponised, he said.

data.title: Eurobattery Minerals AB has received information regarding court judgment and criminal suspicion concerning the CEO
data.description:
EQS-Media / 19.09.2026 / 13:15 CET/CEST

Stockholm, 19 September 2026 – The Board of Directors of Eurobattery Minerals AB (Nordic Growth Market: “BAT” and Börse Stuttgart: “EBM”; hereinafter “Eurobattery Minerals” or the “Company”) hereby announces that the Board has received information that the Company’s CEO and board member, Roberto García Martínez, has been convicted of fraud by a judgment in Spain. The judgment relates to circumstances connected to an investment in a mining operation in Sierra Leone in 2011.

The judgment was subsequently reviewed by the Tribunal Supremo (Supreme Court of Spain), which rendered its judgment on 21 January 2026, and is final. The sentence includes two years’ imprisonment, a fine, and joint and several liability for damages of USD 3.46 million.

A subsequent enforcement decision by the Provincial Court of Bizkaia dated 21 April 2026, as confirmed by a final order dated 29 May 2026, suspended the enforcement of the prison sentence for a probationary period of five years. The suspension is subject to conditions, including monthly payments during the suspension period and payment of 60 per cent of the civil liability amount into the court’s account by the end of that period. Failure to comply with the conditions may result in revocation of the suspension and enforcement of the custodial sentence. The remaining findings of the judgment remain in force.

The Company has furthermore received information that the Swedish Economic Crime Authority (Ekobrottsmyndigheten) has served notice of suspected criminal conduct on Roberto García Martínez in respect of three counts of aggravated insider dealing relating to transactions in the Company’s financial instruments.

The Board is investigating the situation and considering appropriate measures. The Company will provide further information in due course.

Adding to the buzz, a man went viral for claiming that he sold family gold passed down through generations to buy the premium phone for his wife. Industrialist Harsh Goenka shared the man's video on X, expressing his reaction to the man’s claims.

“Some people sell gold to buy a house. Some sell it for their children’s future. data.title: Porsche could face another 4,000 job cuts, Handelsblatt reports
data.description:
Volkswagen's sweeping turnaround plan foresees more than 4,000 further job cuts at Porsche , German business daily Handelsblatt reported on Saturday, following a profit warning linked to problems at the sports car subsidiary.

Files documenting a recent agreement by Volkswagen's supervisory board to usher in the German auto group's largest restructuring yet propose a reduction of "about 4,100 employees" at the brand, addressing an overhead shortfall of some €700 million ($803.8 million), according to Handelsblatt.

The newspaper said the cuts would be "in addition to existing agreements".

In July, Porsche management and labour representatives agreed to an additional 5,000 layoffs on top of 4,000 determined earlier, bringing the scope of currently agreed job cuts at the Stuttgart-based 911 maker to around one in five by 2035.

Volkswagen and Porsche could not immediately be reached for comment. The parent company can only recommend, but not mandate, such measures at Porsche.

Volkswagen on Friday revised down its full-year margin target, now hoping for 1% at best rather than a previous range of 4.0-5.5%.

The revision was due in large part to a writedown at Porsche, whose CEO Michael Leiters is under pressure to deliver a comeback strategy following a collapse in China sales and a costly reversal of the carmaker's EV strategy.($1 = 0.8709 euros)

data.title: China central bank adviser says AI could deepen supply-demand imbalance
data.description:
Artificial intelligence could deepen and prolong China's strong supply and weak demand imbalance, a central bank adviser said on Saturday, adding to calls for policies that bolster consumption and repair balance sheets across the economy.

China's policymakers have been trying to revive domestic demand amid a prolonged property downturn, local government debt pressures and cautious household spending. A global AI boom has helped support China's exports this year, cushioning the economy against weak domestic demand.

"As AI is deployed more widely and innovation accelerates, the imbalance between strong supply and weak demand could worsen," said Huang Yiping, a member of the People's Bank of China's monetary policy committee, at an economic forum held in Beijing.

"The contradiction between total demand and total supply may not disappear quickly in the short term, and may even persist for some time," he added.

The United States and some trading partners have urged Beijing to rebalance its economy towards consumption and away from a reliance on exports, arguing that excess industrial capacity is flooding overseas markets with cheap Chinese goods.

China should further advance market-oriented reforms, allowing markets a greater role in allocating resources and helping increase the share of household income in the economy, Huang said, adding that Beijing should also consider deeper overseas investment and industrial cooperation, rather than relying solely on exports.

Huang proposed that the central government increase borrowing to help repair the balance sheets of local governments, financial institutions and companies.

"Without restoring the capacity of these entities to undertake new economic activity, stimulus policies would have limited effect," Huang said.

data.title: Maruti Suzuki aims to sell 1 million green vehicles in FY27, launches automatic S-CNG range
data.description:
Maruti Suzuki India Ltd (MSIL) is targeting 1 million "green vehicle" sales - spanning CNG, hybrid and EV - this financial year, helped by structural tailwinds such as rising crude prices and the introduction of automatic transmission in CNG variants.

The car market leader, under its Auto Green Mission, on Friday launched automatic S-CNG variants of its popular car models - Swift, Dzire and Baleno.

MSIL, a dominant player in the CNG category with a 70 per cent market share, was earlier expecting sales of 8 to 9 lakh units of green vehicles this fiscal. However, it raised the projection with the introduction of new automatic transmission models, said Senior Executive Officer, Marketing & Sales Partho Banerjee.

He noted thet CNG models previously lost out to petrol/automatic combinations because they lacked automatic transmission options.

The new Swift, Dzire and Baleno automatic S-CNG launches target exactly the "new-age customers who refuse to compromise", buyers who wanted CNG's running-cost benefit but would not give up automatic convenience, he said.

"This opens CNG to a segment that was previously unaddressed," Banerjee said in a media roundtable here.

Replying to a query whether high crude prices, hovering at USD 100 per barrel, will help amplify the adoption of green vehicles, he said: "Yes, no doubt about it. We are aiming for close to almost 1 million sales (FY27)." Maruti Suzuki is banking on its dominant position in the CNG segment to scale up towards the 1 million mark, with the company currently selling close to 80,000 CNG vehicles a month, he said.

Within its own portfolio, CNG penetration stands at around 43 per cent, giving the company a strong base to expand rather than build demand from scratch, Banerjee said.

According to Banerjee, the primary constraint to higher CNG volumes is on the supply side rather than customer demand.

"I have gotten now a capacity restriction on the total CNG vehicles... I am playing with the CNG vehicles by allocating it based on my waiting periods," Banerjee said, adding that as production capacity — currently at 18,000 units a month — is ramped up, the company expects to unlock higher volumes.

"As soon as they are able to further increase the CNG supplies, we can take it to the next level," he said.

Asked if the new launches could push CNG penetration to 50 per cent of the green portfolio, Banerjee said, "If we get the supplies, we are very hopeful... let's keep our fingers crossed" on whether this is achieved within the current fiscal.

MSIL claimed its Dzire automatic S-CNG is India's most fuel-efficient sedan, delivering a fuel efficiency of 36.47 km/kg.

The Dzire automatic S-CNG comes with introductory price of ₹8.53 lakh, the Swift automatic S-CNG at ₹7.92 lakh, and the Baleno automatic S-CNG at ₹8.32 lakh (ex-showroom).

data.title: JSW Energy arm JSW Hydro Energy wins appeal against CERC order on interest claim
data.description:
JSW Energy Ltd on Saturday (September 19) said its material step-down subsidiary JSW Hydro Energy Ltd has secured an order from the Appellate Tribunal for Electricity, which has set aside a Central Electricity Regulatory Commission order and allowed its claim for notional interest during construction.

JSW Hydro Energy had challenged the order dated March 17, 2022, passed by the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission, which had disallowed its claim for notional interest during construction on equity exceeding 30% infused during construction.

The claim relates to the truing-up of tariff for the 2014-19 period and determination of tariff for the 2019-24 period. In its order dated September 18, 2026, the Appellate Tribunal for Electricity allowed the interest during construction claim of JSW Hydro Energy and set aside the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission's order.

The tribunal further held that the carrying cost on the claim shall be reckoned from the date of filing of the true-up petition until its eventual adjustment. The matter has been remanded to the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission to undertake a prudence check of the data submitted in relation to additional interest during construction.

First Quarter Results

The company posted a 36.6% year-on-year decline in reported net profit to ₹471 crore for the quarter ended June, compared with ₹743.1 crore in the corresponding period last year.

Revenue from operations rose 1.2% to ₹5,207.1 crore, while EBITDA increased 3% to ₹2,873.2 crore. EBITDA margin improved to 55.18% from 54.22% a year earlier.

Electricity generation during the quarter stood at 12.9 billion units (BU), down 5% year-on-year, although it improved 10% sequentially. Renewable generation continued to remain the standout performer, rising 11% to 3.4 BU on the back of higher solar and wind output, while thermal generation declined 6% to 8 BU.

Power supplied under long-term power purchase agreements (PPAs) slipped 4% year-on-year to 11.2 BU, while short-term PPA generation fell 7% to 1.6 BU.

Despite softer generation, the company said India witnessed robust electricity demand during the quarter, with nationwide consumption rising 8.5% year-on-year to 483 BU amid an extended heatwave and delayed monsoon. Peak power demand touched a record 271 GW in May before remaining elevated at 265 GW in June.

Shares of JSW Energy Ltd ended at ₹517.80, up by ₹6.80, or 1.33%, on the BSE.

data.title: Nestle India issues clarification: Why FMCG stock plunged? What's FSSAI baby formula row; why it matters to consumers?
data.description:
New Delhi, Sept. 19 -- Nestle India has rejected a recent media report about alleged legal action by the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) over its baby formula products, calling the report "factually incorrect".

Nestle issued the clarification on September 18, 2026, after receiving a query from the stock exchanges regarding a news report published on Moneycontrol the same day. Nestle India said its products, including NAN Excella Pro and Lactogen Pro, comply with applicable regulations.

"Our products are fully compliant with all the applicable regulations. The said products (i.e., NAN EXCELLA PRO & LACTOGEN PRO) and their labels were approved by the expert committee of FSSAI," it said.

The company further informed that it had submitted a detailed response to the authorities regarding statements appearing on the product labels. According to Nestle India, these statements were factual and supported by scientific literature.

Nestle India also reiterated its compliance with regulations covering product labels and declarations. It also said it would continue working with FSSAI on consumer awareness.

"We confirm to adherence of all regulations including all norms and label declarations as per applicable laws. We will continue to work closely and support FSSAI in its efforts towards consumer awareness," said the firm.

The company further pointed out that all material information that could have an impact on its operations or performance had been disclosed to the stock exchanges in accordance with Regulation 30 of the SEBI Listing Regulations. Nestle India stated that such disclosures had been made regularly, accurately and in a timely manner.

Furthermore, responding specifically to the exchange's query on whether there was any undisclosed information that could explain movements in the company's shares, Nestle India said it had no such information to report. The company also said the reported news item had no material impact on the company.

Nestle India also reiterated its compliance with regulations covering product labels and declarations. It also said it would continue working with FSSAI on consumer awareness.

FSSAI had taken regulatory action against Nestle India after identifying multiple compliance issues involving its infant nutrition products. The regulator filed three adjudication cases concerning Infant Nutrition, NAN Excella and Lactogen.

The action followed an examination of the products and their promotional material listed on e-commerce platforms. FSSAI found that NAN Excella Pro Stage 1 carried claims about "5 HMOs" and "Whey Protein", while Lactogen Pro 1 promoted Whey Protein as being easy to digest. The regulator determined that these claims breached provisions restricting promotional material for infant foods under the 2020 regulations and the IMS Act, 1992.

Separately, testing of a Nestle follow-up formula sample found its Biotin content below the prescribed level. A subsequent re-analysis by a referral laboratory also found the sample did not meet the required Biotin standard.

FSSAI said the findings formed part of its broader food-safety enforcement measures. Following the product and laboratory findings, it proceeded with three separate adjudication cases against Nestle India.

Nestle India remained under pressure on Friday, with the FMCG major's stock settling 1.4% lower at Rs.1,353.10 after the FSSAI launched legal action over multiple food safety violations. The regulator filed cases regarding three products, following laboratory tests failing to meet Biotin requirements.

The recent performance has been mixed depending on the time frame. The stock has slipped 3% in the past week and 8% over the last month, while its decline over four months stands at 4%.

Looking at the longer term, however, the stock has retained gains. Nestle India is up 11.5% over six months and has advanced 11% in the past year. Over a five-year period, the stock has delivered a 33% return.

The stock's 52-week trading range has been between Rs.1,145.10 and Rs.1,553. It touched the lower end in October 2025 and reached its 52-week peak in August 2026.

The FSSAI action matters to consumers because the products under scrutiny are infant nutrition products, making questions around their composition and claims. The regulator examined NAN Excella Pro Stage 1 and Lactogen Pro 1, flagging claims related to "5 HMOs", "Whey Protein" and the digestibility of whey protein.

More importantly, FSSAI separately found a sample of a Nestle follow-up formula to be below the prescribed Biotin requirement. A second analysis by a referral laboratory also found the sample non-conforming with the required Biotin level.

For consumers, the episode highlights why accurate nutritional information and regulated claims matter when choosing infant food. At the same time, the proceedings should not be interpreted as a blanket finding that all Nestle infant products are unsafe.

FSSAI has initiated adjudication proceedings, while Nestle India maintains that its products comply with applicable regulations and that the labels in question had been approved by an FSSAI expert committee.

data.title: Tirupati Group Appoints Uday K. Potdar As Chief Financial Officer
data.description:
Potdar brings over two decades of pharmaceutical finance experience, including senior roles at Emcure Pharmaceuticals and Lupin

Tirupati Group has appointed Uday K. Potdar as its new Chief Financial Officer (CFO). He will be based in Paonta Sahib, Himachal Pradesh.

Potdar brings more than 20 years of finance experience in the pharmaceutical industry, with expertise in financial planning and analysis (FP&A), corporate strategy, costing and initial public offering (IPO) execution.

He joins Tirupati Group after a long association with Emcure Pharmaceuticals, where he held several senior finance positions. His roles at the company included Director, Associate Director - Finance & Costing, General Manager - Finance & Costing and Deputy General Manager - Finance.

Most recently, Potdar served as Director at Emcure Pharmaceuticals from April 2024. Before that, he was Associate Director - Finance & Costing from April 2021, following nearly a decade as General Manager - Finance & Costing.

Earlier in his career, Potdar was associated with Lupin, where he gained further experience in the pharmaceutical sector. His professional background includes financial management, FP&A, corporate strategy, costing and IPO execution.

As CFO, Potdar will oversee the finance function at Tirupati Group. The company operates across pharmaceuticals, nutraceuticals, Ayurveda and sports nutrition.

Tirupati Group began operations in 2005 and has research and development and manufacturing facilities in Himachal Pradesh. According to the company, it serves 145 clients across 11 countries and operates in accordance with GLP standards.

The group has businesses spanning pharmaceutical products, nutraceuticals, Ayurveda and sports nutrition, with operations covering research and development and manufacturing.

Potdar's appointment adds a finance executive with more than two decades of pharmaceutical-sector experience to Tirupati Group's leadership team.

data.title: Piyush Pankaj To Take Over As GTPL Hathway CFO From October
data.description:
The company’s strategy and B2B business head succeeds Saurav Banerjee as GTPL Hathway changes its finance leadership from October

GTPL Hathway has appointed Piyush Pankaj as its Chief Financial Officer (CFO), effective 1 October 2026, succeeding Saurav Banerjee, who is set to retire on 30 September. Pankaj, currently Business Head – B2B (CATV & Broadband) and Chief Strategy Officer, has been with the company for around a decade and will move into the finance leadership role amid ongoing investments in digital infrastructure and business expansion.

Internal Finance Transition

Pankaj has held multiple responsibilities at GTPL Hathway, including business leadership across B2B operations and strategy. His elevation to CFO represents an internal transition, with an executive familiar with the company’s operations taking charge of its finance function.

The board approved the appointment at its meeting on 18 September. Pankaj will assume responsibility for the CFO function from 1 October, following Banerjee’s superannuation.

The company has also appointed Ashwinkumar Patel as Company Secretary and Compliance Officer with effect from 19 September, succeeding Shweta Sultania.

CFO Change Amid Investment

Banerjee’s retirement marks a change in the company’s financial leadership as GTPL Hathway continues to invest in its cable television and broadband businesses.

The company reported consolidated total revenue of Rs 1,019.9 crore in Q1 FY27, representing a 12 per cent year-on-year increase. However, consolidated profit after tax declined 78 per cent year-on-year to Rs 2.3 crore during the quarter.

The financial performance comes amid higher infrastructure-related costs, including investments associated with the company’s HITS platform.

Expansion Adds Finance Focus

GTPL Hathway has also completed the acquisition of seven ACT Group digital television businesses for Rs 36.23 crore. The transaction expands its digital television operations and adds integration requirements for the finance and operating teams.

For the incoming CFO, managing the financial implications of such investments will form part of the broader finance agenda. Working capital, capital expenditure, cost management and integration-related spending will remain relevant as the company continues to develop its distribution network.

The board has also appointed Gurjeev Singh Kapoor, CEO of Hathway Cable & Datacom, as an Additional Director, effective 18 September.

Leadership Changes

The latest appointments bring changes across GTPL Hathway’s finance, secretarial and board functions.

Pankaj’s move from strategy and B2B operations to the CFO position places an executive with an existing understanding of the company’s business model at the centre of its financial management. Banerjee’s retirement closes his tenure as CFO, while Patel’s appointment changes the company’s secretarial leadership.

Pankaj will take charge as GTPL Hathway navigates the next phase of investment in broadband and digital television while managing profitability pressures following the decline in Q1 FY27 earnings.

data.title: Uttam Sugar Mills Names New CFO After 20-Year Tenure
data.description:
Harish Kumar Dhingra takes charge from 18 September following Sanjay Bhandari’s resignation on health grounds

Uttam Sugar Mills has appointed Harish Kumar Dhingra as Chief Financial Officer (CFO), effective 18 September, following the resignation of Sanjay Bhandari, who held the position for nearly two decades. Dhingra, an internal finance executive who has been with the company since 2005, moves into the role at a time when the sugar producer is facing near-term pressure on profitability.

Internal Finance Succession

Dhingra was serving as General Manager – Finance before his elevation to CFO. He brings more than three decades of experience in finance and corporate operations and has spent over 20 years with Uttam Sugar Mills.

He joined the company in 2005 as Assistant Manager and was elevated to General Manager – Finance in July 2017. His experience covers financial accounting, management and corporate operations.

The appointment provides continuity within the finance function following Bhandari’s departure.

Bhandari Steps Down

Bhandari resigned from the CFO position citing health and medical reasons. He was relieved of his responsibilities on 16 September, bringing an end to a tenure of nearly 20 years in the role.

The company appointed Dhingra as his successor within two days of Bhandari’s exit. The transition also coincides with Uttam Sugar Mills’ 31st Annual General Meeting held on 18 September.

The change in finance leadership comes as the company manages the cyclical nature of the sugar business alongside its distillery and power operations.

Profitability Under Pressure

Uttam Sugar Mills reported consolidated revenue from operations of Rs 2,209.92 crore in FY26, marking a 19.19 per cent year-on-year increase. Consolidated net profit rose 17.24 per cent to Rs 100.59 crore during the year.

The company, however, reported a sharp decline in profitability during Q1 FY27. Consolidated net profit fell 91.05 per cent year-on-year to Rs 1.30 crore, reflecting pressure on margins during the quarter.

The new CFO therefore takes charge against a backdrop of weaker near-term profitability and the seasonal dynamics of the sugar industry.

Focus On Financial Management

Dhingra’s immediate responsibilities will include overseeing the company’s financial function as it enters the next sugarcane crushing cycle. Working capital management, capital allocation and financial planning will remain important as the company balances its sugar operations with its distillery and ethanol-related activities.

His elevation also keeps the finance leadership within the existing management structure, with an executive familiar with the company’s operations taking over after Bhandari’s long tenure.

The CFO transition comes at an important point in the company’s operating cycle, with the performance of the upcoming crushing season and movement in input costs likely to remain relevant to its financial performance.

data.title: Nitish Mittersain And The Astrology Of Reinvention
data.description:
From surviving the dot-com crash to building Nazara into a listed global gaming and media portfolio, Vikkramm Chandirramani traces the planetary periods that have accompanied Mittersain’s entrepreneurial journey and considers what may come next

Nitish Mittersain belongs to the small group of Indian entrepreneurs who began building for the digital economy before the market around them was ready.

A computer enthusiast from an early age, he started coding games while still in school. His first venture, Internet 3000, provided websites to companies during the early years of the internet in India. After completing his BCom from Sydenham College of Commerce and Economics, he incorporated Nazara Technologies on 8 December 1999, when he was just 20.

The timing was bold. It was also unforgiving.

The dot-com crash arrived soon afterwards, taking down several young internet businesses. Nazara survived, but Mittersain has spoken about the company being left with debt of around Rs 3 crore to Rs 4 crore and virtually no revenue. The years that followed became an early test of his ability to adapt, rebuild and continue investing in an industry whose commercial future was still uncertain.

From an astrological perspective, this entrepreneurial journey began during his Mars mahadasha, which commenced in May 1998.

An Entrepreneurial Chart

Mittersain’s natal chart has Virgo rising, with the Sun, Mars and Ketu placed in Aquarius. The Moon is in Aries, Mercury in Pisces, Jupiter in Cancer, Venus in Capricorn and Saturn with Rahu in Leo.

Virgo rising is often associated with analytical thinking, attention to detail and a methodical approach to problem-solving. Aquarius adds an instinct for technology, networks and unconventional business models. The Aries Moon contributes initiative, competitiveness and a willingness to move before consensus has formed.

Jupiter is exalted in Cancer, indicating the potential for growth through knowledge, capital allocation, partnerships and institution-building. Venus in Capricorn suggests discipline in financial matters and an ability to create value through structure rather than spectacle.

The chart also contains a strong opposition between the Sun and Saturn. Such an alignment can create repeated encounters with authority, regulation and institutional resistance. At the same time, it can produce an individual who learns to work through complexity rather than retreat from it.

These combinations help explain the defining features of Mittersain’s professional life: an early attraction to technology, a willingness to take calculated risks and an ability to reinvent the business as the market changes.

Building Through Sade Sati

Nazara was incorporated during the Mars-Jupiter period. Mars provided entrepreneurial energy, while Jupiter supported ambition, expansion and the desire to build something of scale.

However, Mittersain was also passing through the period astrologers describe as Sade Sati, associated with Saturn’s transit around the natal Moon. This period is frequently misunderstood as being entirely negative. In practice, it can coincide with extraordinary responsibility, disruption and achievement.

Several prominent figures have experienced major breakthroughs during Sade Sati. Narendra Modi became Prime Minister in 2014, Donald Trump won the US presidency in 2016 and Tesla completed its initial public offering in 2010, during Elon Musk’s Sade Sati.

For Mittersain, the period brought both the creation of Nazara and the dot-com collapse. The company’s survival established a pattern that would recur throughout his career: pressure followed by reinvention.

The business initially focused on online gaming, but the Indian internet market was not yet large enough to support the model. Nazara subsequently changed its name in July 2003 and began developing Java-based mobile games distributed through telecom operators.

By 2004, the company was working with operators such as BPL and Hutch. Deals involving Sachin Tendulkar and later MS Dhoni helped connect mobile gaming with cricket and celebrity-led intellectual property. WestBridge Capital’s investment gave the company institutional backing at a time when the Indian gaming sector was still at an early stage.

The Rahu Years

Mittersain entered his Rahu mahadasha in May 2005. In Vedic astrology, Rahu is associated with technology, mass markets, foreign relationships, rapid expansion and unconventional opportunities. Its influence can produce dramatic progress, although rarely in a predictable or linear manner.

The Rahu-Rahu period coincided with Nazara expanding its distribution relationships with Tata Teleservices, Vodafone and Bharti Airtel. WestBridge invested in the company in 2007, strengthening its capacity to grow.

During the Rahu-Jupiter phase, from January 2008 to June 2010, Nazara entered into an arrangement with Electronic Arts for the distribution of mobile games in India. It also launched a games club in partnership with Reliance Communications.

The Rahu-Saturn period, from June 2010 to April 2013, pushed the company towards international markets. Nazara expanded into Dubai and established entities across Singapore, Mauritius and several African markets. Bangladesh followed in 2014.

From April 2013 to November 2015, during Rahu-Mercury, the company shifted towards the freemium gaming model and added celebrity and entertainment properties associated with Virat Kohli, Hrithik Roshan and Chhota Bheem.

Mittersain also stepped away from the chief executive’s role during this period, beginning his transition from being solely an operator to becoming a strategic investor and portfolio builder.

From Gaming Company To Gaming Portfolio

The Rahu-Venus phase, from November 2016 to November 2019, marked the emergence of Nazara’s acquisition-led strategy.

The company invested in or acquired businesses including Next Wave Multimedia, Nodwin Gaming, Halaplay, Sports Unity, Absolute Sports, which operates Sportskeeda, and Paper Boat Apps, the developer of Kiddopia.

Each transaction extended Nazara into a different part of the gaming, sports media, esports or learning ecosystem. The company was no longer dependent on a single game, distribution channel or business model.

Nazara converted into a public limited company in 2017 and made an initial attempt to access the capital markets in 2018. The listing did not take place then, but the process prepared the company for a later opportunity.

The Rahu-Moon period ultimately brought Nazara to the public markets. In February 2021, the company raised Rs 100 crore in pre-IPO capital. Its public issue opened in March and was subscribed more than 175 times.

The shares were issued at Rs 1,101 and listed on the NSE at around Rs 1,990, a premium of approximately 81 per cent.

The IPO was entirely an offer for sale. Mittersain did not sell his personal stake, although promoter entity Mitter Infotech participated in the offering. Investors associated with the company included Rakesh Jhunjhunwala, Utpal Sheth, IIFL, WestBridge and Plutus Wealth.

The Rahu-Mars period, from April 2022 to May 2023, brought Mittersain back into a more direct executive role. He returned as chief executive in October 2022, at a time when the company was expanding its portfolio and preparing for another stage of growth.

The Jupiter Phase

Mittersain entered his Jupiter mahadasha on 2 May 2023.

Jupiter is particularly significant in his chart because it is exalted in Cancer and connected with professional growth. Its mahadasha can widen the scale of ambition, increase access to capital and shift the individual’s role from building a business to directing an ecosystem.

The Jupiter-Jupiter period, which continued until June 2025, coincided with significant capital raising and portfolio expansion.

In January 2024, Nazara raised Rs 250 crore at Rs 872.15 per share. A broader round included investments of Rs 410 crore from SBI Mutual Fund and Rs 100 crore from entities associated with the Kamath brothers.

In November 2024, the company issued shares worth approximately Rs 855 crore at Rs 954.27 per share. In June 2025, Axana Estates invested Rs 495 crore through the acquisition of 50 lakh shares at Rs 990 each.

The acquisition strategy also widened. Nazara added Comic Con India, Branded, Ninja Global, Starladder, Freaks 4U Gaming, Fusebox Games and stakes in several other businesses. Paper Boat Apps became wholly owned, while the company increased its position in Absolute Sports and Next Wave Multimedia.

Moonshine Technology, which operates PokerBaazi, became another important investment. However, the subsequent regulatory shift affecting real-money gaming in India demonstrated the risks attached to operating in a policy-sensitive sector.

The period also involved portfolio discipline. Nazara exited or reduced its involvement in businesses that no longer fitted its strategic direction. Some companies were sold, while others, including Nodwin Gaming, ceased to be consolidated after changes in ownership and control.

This combination of buying, selling, consolidating and deconsolidating reflects an important change in Mittersain’s role. He is increasingly acting as a capital allocator rather than the manager of a single operating business.

The BestPlay Acquisition

One of the most significant developments came in 2026, during the Jupiter-Saturn period.

In March, Nazara announced an in-principle agreement to acquire 50 per cent of Bluetile and BestPlay. By August, the transaction had expanded into the proposed acquisition of the entire business for $303.02 million in cash.

BestPlay and Bluetile collectively reported revenue of $153.6 million for calendar year 2025. The transaction became the largest acquisition of Mittersain’s operating career and represented a decisive step towards building Nazara as an international gaming platform.

The acquisition was accompanied by a leadership transition. The board accepted Mittersain’s resignation as chief executive with effect from 1 September 2026. Raymond Albaladejo Stauffer, the founder of Bluetile and BestPlay, was appointed chief executive, subject to the required approvals.

Mittersain continues as founder and managing director, with responsibility for strategy, portfolio direction, organisational culture and key stakeholder relationships.

This change is consistent with the wider arc of his chart. Jupiter expands the canvas, while Saturn encourages structure, delegation and institution-building. The task is no longer merely to operate the company. It is to create a system capable of growing beyond its founder.

Investor Beyond Nazara

Mittersain’s investment activity extends beyond Nazara Technologies.

His personal portfolio has included companies such as Rentomojo, myHQ, Zenduty and Biryani By Kilo. Several of these investments have since progressed towards acquisitions or public-market activity.

These are personal investments and should not be confused with Nazara’s corporate portfolio. However, they reveal the same underlying approach: backing technology-led or consumer-focused businesses, supporting them through different stages of development and remaining open to strategic exits.

The distinction becomes increasingly important as Mittersain’s professional identity expands. He is still closely associated with Nazara, but his future may involve a wider range of investments, acquisitions and institution-building initiatives undertaken independently of the company.

A Career Defined By Reinvention

Mittersain’s career can be understood through a series of distinct phases.

Mars supported the founding of Nazara and the determination required to survive its early crisis. Rahu brought technology, telecom distribution, international expansion, acquisitions and the public listing. Jupiter has so far brought larger pools of capital, international assets and a shift towards portfolio-level leadership.

The corporate milestones tell the same story in business language.

Nazara began as an online gaming company, moved into mobile distribution, embraced freemium gaming, assembled a portfolio across esports, sports media and gamified learning, entered the public markets and then began expanding through international acquisitions.

Few Indian technology companies have reinvented their operating model as many times while maintaining continuity of ownership and strategic direction.

What May Come Next

data.title: Karnataka HC Upholds ED Seizure Of Genpact Property In FEMA Case
data.description:
Karnataka High Court says ED had sufficient grounds to seize Genpact’s Gurgaon property under FEMA, while leaving the question of an actual violation to the competent authority.

The Karnataka High Court has upheld the Enforcement Directorate's action to seize a Genpact property in Gurgaon under India's foreign exchange law, finding that the agency had sufficient material to form a "reason to believe" that warranted action under the Foreign Exchange Management Act.

The ruling, delivered on September 16 by Justice Suraj Govindaraj, relates to a series of transactions involving Genpact India and its overseas group companies in 2015, followed by payments running into thousands of crores from India to overseas entities.

The court, however, made clear that it was not deciding whether Genpact had ultimately violated FEMA. That determination will have to be made by the competent authority under Section 37A of the law.

At the centre of the Enforcement Directorate's investigation are transactions involving Empower India, Genpact India and overseas Genpact entities.

According to the judgment, Genpact Bermuda borrowed USD 737.5 million from Morgan Stanley in March 2015. The funds were routed through Genpact Luxembourg, which subscribed to 4,600 non-convertible debentures issued by Empower India for about Rs 4,600 crore.

Empower India transferred the entire amount on the same day to acquire the remaining 51 per cent stake in Genpact India. The funds were subsequently transferred to Genpact Singapore and then Genpact Bermuda, which used the money to repay the Morgan Stanley borrowing.

The ED argued that the transactions formed part of a connected arrangement and amounted to a circular movement of funds.

The court held that the agency was entitled to examine the transactions as a connected arrangement rather than considering each transaction separately.

The judgment also records that Genpact India made payments of around Rs 7,800 crore to Genpact Luxembourg between 2018 and 2023 towards repayment of the principal and interest on the non-convertible debentures.

The court said these subsequent transactions could be examined as part of the arrangement under investigation, even though Section 37A could not be applied retrospectively to transactions that took place before the provision came into force.

On the seizure of Genpact's Gurgaon property, the court found that the ED's order contained sufficient material for the authorised officer to form the requisite "reason to believe" under Section 37A.

"At this stage, the court is not called upon to determine whether there is a contravention of FEMA," the judgment said, adding that the issue would have to be decided by the competent authority.

Genpact had also pointed to proceedings involving the Reserve Bank of India, the Securities and Exchange Board of India and income-tax authorities.

The High Court said those proceedings did not prevent the ED from independently examining the transactions under FEMA, noting that they had not determined whether the entire arrangement, viewed as a whole, constituted a violation of Section 4 of FEMA.

The court therefore dismissed Genpact's challenge to the seizure.

It did, however, set aside the ED's rejection of Genpact's application for a no-objection certificate for a proposed USD 100 million investment in its GIFT City entity.

The court directed the competent authority to reconsider the application and issue a reasoned order.

The ED was represented by Additional Solicitor General N. Venkataraman and other counsel, including Senior Advocate Madhu N. Rao.

data.title: Adani Ports, JSW Infra, Essar Ports Vie For Rs 5,881 Cr Dadri Logistics Hub
data.description:
The greenfield multimodal logistics hub in Greater Noida will be developed in three phases with a planned capacity of 1.44 million TEUs and 7.8 million tonnes of non-containerised cargo

Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone, JSW Infrastructure and Essar Ports have submitted initial bids for a Rs 5,881 crore greenfield Multi Modal Logistics Hub (MMLH) at Dadri in Greater Noida, Uttar Pradesh.

The tender has been floated by DMIC Integrated Industrial Township Greater Noida, a special-purpose vehicle formed by the National Industrial Corridor Development and Implementation Trust (NICDIT) and the Greater Noida Development Authority (GNIDA). This marks the second attempt in the past year to develop the large-scale logistics facility.

Three-Phase Development

Spread across 311 hectares, the logistics hub will provide mechanised warehousing, specialised storage, cargo handling and intermodal transfer facilities for containerised, bulk and break-bulk cargo.

The project will be developed in three phases over a 45-year concession period. The first phase entails an investment of Rs 2,374 crore and will provide capacity to handle 0.74 million twenty-foot equivalent units (TEUs) and 6.7 million tonnes of non-containerised cargo.

The second phase, involving Rs 1,412 crore, will increase capacity to 1.12 million TEUs and 7.2 million tonnes of non-containerised cargo. The final phase, requiring Rs 2,095 crore, will take capacity to 1.44 million TEUs and 7.8 million tonnes.

Warehousing And Cold Storage

The facility will also include modern warehousing and cold storage infrastructure. The private developer will create 3 million sq ft of warehousing space and 0.3 million sq ft of cold storage capacity in the first phase.

Warehousing capacity can subsequently rise to 4 million sq ft and 5.5 million sq ft in the second and third phases, respectively, while cold storage capacity is planned to increase to 0.4 million sq ft and 0.5 million sq ft.

The hub will also offer value-added services such as cross-docking, customisation, stacking and labelling.

Strategic Freight Connectivity

The Dadri project is positioned at the junction of the Eastern and Western Dedicated Freight Corridors, giving it access to major freight routes connecting northern India with ports and industrial centres.

The facility will also have direct connectivity to NH34, the Eastern Peripheral Expressway and Jewar International Airport. It is located adjacent to the Delhi-Howrah broad-gauge railway line and old NH-91.

The location is expected to enable the hub to tap freight traffic on both dedicated freight corridors and support industrial and distribution activity across the National Capital Region and its hinterland.

Bidder To Be Selected On Revenue Share

The project will be awarded to the bidder offering the highest Minimum Guaranteed Revenue Share to the project authority.

The private concessionaire will be responsible for developing, operating, maintaining and managing the logistics hub, including its commercial and ancillary facilities. The project is expected to strengthen multimodal freight movement and improve logistics efficiency in the Greater Noida-Dadri industrial belt.

data.title: MICE & Business Events Push Hotel Demand & Rates Higher Across India In September
data.description:
Hotel operators and travel platforms report higher bookings, occupancies and room rates as business events, exhibitions, MICE activity and government movement drive demand across key Indian markets

India’s hotel market is seeing a strong September, with corporate travel, MICE activity, government movement, exhibitions and major business events contributing to higher demand across metros and large tier-two cities.

The increase is particularly visible in Delhi, where the BRICS Summit has added significant pressure on room inventory and rates, while Mumbai and other business destinations are also benefiting from a busy events calendar. Recent industry reports have highlighted sharp increases in Delhi hotel prices and tightening availability around the September 12-13 BRICS Summit.

According to Bhanu Chopra, Founder and Managing Director, RateGain Travel Technologies, bookings through RateGain's platform increased 36 per cent by volume and 82 per cent by value during the first eight days of September compared with the same period in August.

The difference between booking volume and value points to a shift towards larger and longer reservations. Chopra attributes part of this movement to conference and exhibition demand.

Travel and hospitality management company CoTrav is also seeing increased activity. Vinod Kumar Sah, Co-founder and Chief Technology Officer, says corporate events, MICE and travel activity from existing clients has grown by 20-30 per cent through the year into September, while activity from new clients has risen 50 per cent during the month.

“Overall, our September business is up by over 70 per cent compared to September 2025,” Sah says.

Hotel performance indicators are also reflecting the increase in demand. Animesh Kumar, Commercial Head, Ibis and Ibis Styles, says occupancy across the brands' Indian properties during the first 10 days of September was up 8-10 per cent, while average daily rates increased 16-18 per cent compared with the same period last year.

The movement is particularly pronounced in markets with strong corporate and events calendars. Mumbai has benefited from the Global Fintech Fest 2026, held from September 8 to 11, while Delhi's event calendar includes Semicon India 2026 from September 17 to 19.

Delhi has also experienced a significant rate increase around the BRICS Summit. Cleartrip reports that luxury hotel rates in the capital rose 59 per cent year-on-year, while four-star hotel rates increased by around 113 per cent. Budget bookings were also reported to be up 138 per cent from a year earlier.

Independent coverage around the summit has similarly pointed to limited room availability and substantial increases in Delhi's luxury hotel rates, with some properties quoting rates above ₹2 lakh per night during the peak period.

Bharatt Malik, Senior Vice President, Air and Hotel Business, Yatra Online, says commercial exhibitions and MICE events are supporting demand in Mumbai, with core hotels recording an increase of around 5 per cent in booking volumes.

The impact of MICE is extending beyond the major metros. Gajesh Girdhar, Chairman, Governing Council and Founder Member, Network of Indian MICE Agents, says MICE rates across India have increased 10-15 per cent year-on-year.

“A lot of events have stayed in India as people are less interested in hosting events overseas,” Girdhar says, pointing to destinations including Udaipur, Jaipur, Srinagar, Mumbai, Bhubaneswar and Goa as markets likely to see increased rates as MICE demand rises.

The trend also reflects the growing role of domestic destinations in India's business-events ecosystem. As companies and organisers evaluate destinations for conferences, incentives and exhibitions, hotels in established MICE markets are benefiting from a combination of corporate movement and event-led travel.

In Delhi, hotels are expecting the strong demand to extend beyond the peak BRICS dates. The LaLiT New Delhi is anticipating a sold-out period around the summit, while General Manager Vishal Sharma says the wider September calendar is also supporting hotel performance.

“Compared to several other months, September is expected to perform strongly in terms of occupancies and rates supported by international business travel, government and corporate movement and the overall calendar of events in the capital,” Sharma says.

For India's hotel sector, the September performance highlights the impact that a concentrated business and events calendar can have on room demand and pricing. With corporate travel, exhibitions, conferences, government movement and MICE activity converging across multiple markets, event-led travel is emerging as an important contributor to hotel performance.

The trend is particularly visible in Delhi and Mumbai, but the wider movement across destinations such as Udaipur, Jaipur, Srinagar, Bhubaneswar and Goa points to a broader opportunity for India's hospitality sector as business events increasingly drive travel beyond traditional corporate hubs.

data.title: Havells Adds Motion To Ganpati OOH With Interactive Festive Hoarding
data.description:
Executed by Posterscope India, the festive outdoor installation uses a moving swing, 3D elements and Havells Wires branding to create a visual Ganpati experience

The festive season has prompted Havells India to take its Ganpati communication beyond a conventional billboard, with a kinetic OOH execution that brings motion to the outdoor format.

Executed by Posterscope India, the installation features Lord Ganesha seated on a traditional swing, with the swing designed to move within the advertising unit. The use of 3D elements adds depth to the visual while the movement creates a more dynamic interaction with audiences passing the hoarding.

The execution combines the festive visual with Havells' brand presence. The Havells logo is positioned alongside the installation, while the lower section carries the message गणपती बाप्पा मोरया. Havells Wires products are also integrated into the creative, connecting the festive setting back to the brand's product portfolio.

The installation uses the physicality of OOH to turn a traditionally static advertising format into a moving visual. Rather than relying solely on a festive graphic, the swing introduces a kinetic element designed to catch attention in a busy outdoor environment.

The execution also comes as Posterscope India continues to explore OOH formats that turn everyday physical spaces into more noticeable brand moments. The agency's recent work has included experiential and location-based OOH executions across different consumer contexts.

For Havells, the Ganpati activation combines a familiar cultural cue with a format-led innovation, using movement and three-dimensionality to give its festive communication greater physical presence on the streets.

The result is a festive OOH execution where the cultural visual remains at the centre, while the moving installation provides an additional layer of engagement.

data.title: Shekhar Ramarajan Named CEO Of Areion Finserve
data.description:
Nearly 25 years of experience across banking, NBFCs, risk management, lending and financial services leadership

Shekhar Ramarajan has been appointed Chief Executive Officer at Areion Finserve, the NBFC arm of Areion Group, bringing nearly 25 years of experience across banking, NBFCs, housing finance, retail lending, corporate banking and risk management. A Chartered Accountant, Ramarajan has held leadership positions spanning business operations, credit, underwriting, risk and portfolio management.

Leadership At KVB

Ramarajan joins Areion Finserve after serving as General Manager and Head – Corporate & Institutional Group at Karur Vysya Bank. During his tenure with the bank, he also held leadership responsibilities as Head – Retail Assets, Chief Risk Officer and National Credit and Operations Manager – KVB NEO.

His experience at the bank covered business leadership, credit operations, risk management and retail assets, giving him exposure to multiple segments of financial services and lending.

Diverse Financial Services Experience

Before his tenure at Karur Vysya Bank, Ramarajan held leadership roles across housing finance and lending businesses. His professional journey includes stints with Aditya Birla Housing Finance, Aditya Birla Capital Finance, Manappuram Finance and Kotak Mahindra Bank.

Across these roles, he has worked across retail lending, corporate banking, underwriting, commercial real estate and financial risk. His experience also includes managing large portfolios and leading teams across different business functions.

Focus On Business Growth

In his new role as CEO, Ramarajan will lead the NBFC business at Areion Finserve. His background combines business development and portfolio management with experience in credit, governance, compliance and enterprise risk frameworks.

His appointment brings experience from both banking and non-banking financial services to the leadership of the company. His earlier roles have involved managing business portfolios, developing financial solutions and overseeing risk and credit functions.

Experience Across Key Functions

Ramarajan's career has included responsibilities spanning business leadership, credit, operations, risk and underwriting. This cross-functional experience has provided exposure to different stages of the lending and financial services cycle.

His move to Areion Finserve marks a transition into the chief executive role after a career across established banking, housing finance and NBFC institutions. The appointment adds a senior financial services professional with experience across business and risk functions to the company's leadership team.
